item.title: David May, Grammy Winning Producer and Warner Music Executive, Dies at 68
item.description:
[Elegiac music fades out, and the host's voice takes over]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we celebrate the lives and legacies of music industry legends. Today, we're remembering David May, a two-time Grammy Award-winning producer and longtime executive with Warner Music Group, who passed away on April 13th at the age of 68.
[Soft music plays in the background]
Host: David May was a highly respected figure in the music industry, known for his creative vision, technical expertise, and passion for archival preservation. He worked with an incredible array of artists, including Metallica, Eric Clapton, Neil Young, and Madonna, to name just a few.
[Clip of one of the mentioned artists plays for a few seconds]
Host: May's career spanned decades, from his early days as a recording engineer in the 1970s to his work on live concerts and MTV promo videos. He won two Grammy Awards for Best Long Form Music Video, first in 1998 for Alanis Morissette's "Jagged Little Pill, Live" and again in 2008 for Madonna's "The Confessions Tour" concert film.
[Clip of one of the Grammy-winning projects plays]
Host: In addition to his work behind the scenes, David May was also a talented recording artist and songwriter, releasing several original albums and landing syncs on popular TV shows like "American Horror Story" and "The Sinner".
[Soft music continues to play]
Host: David May is survived by his wife Michelle, daughters Alex and Devin, and a legacy that will be remembered by music fans around the world. If you'd like to make a donation in his name, you can do so at the Young Musicians' Foundation in Los Angeles or Siloam Health in Nashville, both of which support underserved communities.
[Music fades out, and the host's voice takes over]
Host: That's all for today's tribute to David May. Thank you for joining us, and we'll be back with more stories from the world of music soon.
